QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_50

question.text: 'Karnataka Seed Category I AIF' is negotiating a pre-money valuation of INR 40 crore for a Seed round investing INR 10 crore (thus post-money = INR 50 crore, AIF stake = 20%). The founders want a 10% option pool created. If the option pool is created PRE-MONEY (absorbed by founders, so the INR 40 crore pre-money is inclusive of the new pool), what stake does the AIF end up with in the post-money cap table?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the stem's assumption that the option pool is created within the pre-money valuation, the founders absorb the option-pool dilution. The post-money cap table therefore has founders plus the new option pool together holding 80%, and the AIF holding INR 10 crore / INR 50 crore = 20%. The AIF stake is unchanged at 20%. The Trap: 18% would arise if the option pool were created post-money (the AIF would then share the dilution). 22% has no supported arithmetic basis. 10% conflates the option-pool size with the AIF's ownership. Note: Option-pool dilution is discussed on pages 231-232 and pre-money / post-money valuation is defined on page 270; the workbook does not quantify a market-standard size for the founders-absorb mechanism.
